blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The implementation re-pinned at Ethereum block 26196960 is StakedUSDf, which exposes setRestrictedStatus and redistributeLockedAmount to DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE. Deposits reject restricted callers and receivers; withdrawals reject restricted callers, receivers and owners. Administrators can burn restricted shares or transfer them to TREASURY. Ordinary ERC-20 transfers have no local isRestricted hook; the direct seizure and deposit/withdrawal controls still establish blacklistability. The transparent-proxy upgrade path can replace token logic. Parent USDf controls remain inherited.

oracleRisk.summary: Native sUSDf mint/redemption conversion uses onchain USDf balances less unvested rewards, not an external feed. Falcon publishes Chainlink-style sUSDf/USDf (0xe471bc940aa9831a0aea21e6f40c1a1236eb4bb3) and USDf/USD (0xb177857a1799aa5f7feb5799fdf12cbe8fdf78b1) aggregators. At Ethereum block 26196960 (2026-10-15T09:16:59Z; https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/), latestRoundData answers were 1138425522042670886 (18dp, updatedAt 1792039679) and 99622819 (8dp, updatedAt 1791990947). These informational/market integrations do not set the native unwrap rate; no borrower-liquidation branch exists in the exact savings implementation. Oracleless describes this local share conversion, not the parent's offchain collateral valuations or hedges.

branchApplicability.rationale: The ERC-4626 share-to-underlying exchange rate is the top-level mint/redemption authority. There are no borrower-owned collateral branches on the savings token.
